title: The story of Yharnam
intro: Start here: the whole story in order, from the people who dug the labyrinth to the night you arrive. Each step names the tour that tells its part in depth. The game never gives dates, so the order between some steps is an inference.

steps.note: Before Yharnam, there were the Pthumerians, "superhuman beings" who carved out the old labyrinth under the city and are said to have unlocked "the wisdom of the eldritch Truth".

The early Pthumerians were "humble guardians of the slumbering Great Ones". The Great Ones were already there, asleep below, long before any human went looking for them. (Tour: The Pthumerians and the chalices.)
Much later, young scholars of Byrgenwerth, a college by a lake, went down into this "tomb of the gods" and found a "holy medium" deep within it: the old blood. (Tour: Byrgenwerth and the Old Blood.)
The blood seemed to deliver what Byrgenwerth dreamed of: "The discovery of blood made their dream of evolution a reality." The rune warns that metamorphosis was "only the beginning".
Master Willem came to fear the blood and its effects. His student Laurence left anyway. "By the gods, fear it, Laurence." Willem's caution and Laurence's ambition shape everything that follows.

Laurence became the first vicar of the Healing Church, which spread the blood as medicine and sacrament: blood ministration. Blood Saints like Adella lend the Church its legitimacy. (Tour: The Healing Church.)

Somewhere in that era, Byrgenwerth committed a crime at a fishing village by the sea, where the Great One Kos had washed ashore. The priest names the culprits and curses them "and their children, and their children's children, for evermore".

That curse never ended. Dying, Simon says the village is "the true secret", "testament to the old sins", and that "it feeds this Hunter's Nightmare", where blood-drunk hunters end up. (Tour: The Hunter's Nightmare.)

steps.text: The nameless moon presence beckoned by…
steps.note: Laurence and his associates also made contact with a Great One themselves: a "nameless moon presence". They called it Paleblood. Its encounter "conceived the Hunter's Dream", the dream you wake up in. (Tour: Paleblood and the Moon.)

The Dream became a workshop and "safe haven for hunters", kept by Gehrman, the first hunter. The Church soon fielded its own hunters, and its executioners purged the Vilebloods of Cainhurst. (Tour: Cainhurst and the Vilebloods.)
The blood caught up with the Church's founder. Laurence, first vicar, "in reality became the first cleric beast". The scourge of beasts was the price of blood ministration.

steps.text: When the hunt began, the Healing…
steps.note: When the scourge broke out, the Church blocked the bridge and let Old Yharnam burn "to the ground that moonlit night". Since then, every night of the hunt, hunters roam the streets. (Tour: The scourge of beasts.)

Meanwhile the Church's upper echelons kept reaching for the Great Ones. The School of Mensis wore these cages as antennas to the Great Ones of the dream, and they "delivered them to their harrowing nightmare". (Tours: The Choir and the cosmos; Mensis and the Nightmare of Mensis.)

steps.text: When the red moon hangs low,…
steps.note: Micolash says their "sacred rite nears completion", and over this night the moon turns red. A note warns: "When the red moon hangs low, the line between man and beast is blurred. And when the Great Ones descend, a womb will be blessed with child." (Tour: Oedon and the Great Ones' children.)
This is the night you arrive: an outsider seeking Paleblood. "Yharnam is the home of blood ministration. You need only unravel its mystery." Your first act is to take Yharnam's blood.

At the end of the night, Gehrman offers mercy: "You will die, forget the dream, and awake under the morning sun." Whether you accept is the game's last choice, and it is decided in cutscenes this map cannot show.

title: The Pthumerians and the chalices
intro: Under Yharnam lies a labyrinth older than the city. A tour of the people who carved it, the queen who ruled them, and the chalices that open it again.

steps.note: Hunters open the old labyrinth with chalices, in a ritual at the tomb altar of the Hunter's Dream: "Let the chalice reveal the tomb of the gods; let blood be the hunter's nourishment."
Gehrman explains where chalices come from: most "lie deep within the tomb of the gods", and the few brought up "were lost again in the hands of men". One is still worshipped in Old Yharnam.
The labyrinth was "carved out by the Pthumerians, superhuman beings that are said to have unlocked the wisdom of the eldritch Truth".

The Pthumerians began as "humble guardians of the slumbering Great Ones". Their descendants grew proud enough to name themselves a leader, and Pthumeru Ihyll became the title of both their monarch and their capital.
That monarch "was traditionally a woman who assumed a name with classical roots".
One of these queens was called Yharnam, like the city built above her tombs. "The Queen lies dead, but her horrific consciousness is only asleep, and stirs in unsettling motions."
The labyrinth is not abandoned. Its Watchers keep digging: "To this day, the Watchers continue to expand the hintertombs", catacombs "filled with graves and death".

Deeper lie other lands. In ailing Loran, there are "trace remains of medical procedures": attempts to control the scourge of the beast, "or the cause of the outbreak". The text says nobody knows. (Tour: The scourge of beasts.)
Further still is Isz, which according to the Choir "lies in contact with the cosmos", allowing the Great Ones "to function on transcendental planes of thought".
Bringing this chalice to the surface, the first since Byrgenwerth's time, gave the Choir its audience with Ebrietas. (Tour: The Choir and the cosmos.)
That is why the Church kept sending prospectors down: the ruins "hide the very secrets of the old Great Ones". (Tour: Byrgenwerth and the Old Blood.)

title: Byrgenwerth and the Old Blood
intro: Where it all begins: a college by a lake, a labyrinth under the city, and a discovery its own master came to fear.

steps.note: Below Yharnam lies an old labyrinth, "the tomb of the gods". Alfred tells how young scholars of Byrgenwerth found a "holy medium" deep inside it.
The Healing Church later sent its own prospectors into those ruins. The Church, this text says, traces its roots to Byrgenwerth, and knows the ruins hide the secrets of the Great Ones.
Byrgenwerth's master, Willem, had an epiphany: humans think "on the basest of planes", and what they need are "more eyes".
One of Willem's students, Caryll, transcribed the inhuman sounds of the Great Ones into runes. Willem would have approved: they "do not rely upon blood in any measure".
Another student, Laurence, takes his leave of Willem. They share an adage, "Fear the old blood", but Laurence leaves anyway.
Willem's reply: the blood "makes us human, makes us more than human, makes us human no more". The rest of his words show what his own search for eyes has made of him.

steps.text: Master Willem was right. Evolution without…
steps.note: A note left in the game: whoever wrote it sided with Willem's caution against Laurence's ambition. Laurence's path leads to the next tour, the Healing Church.

title: The Healing Church
intro: Yharnam is "the home of blood ministration". Follow the Church that made blood a sacrament, from its first vicar to its hunters.

steps.note: The game opens with this promise to an outsider: Yharnam is the home of blood ministration, and you only need a contract and "a bit of Yharnam blood of your own".
Ministration is ordinary medicine in Yharnam: each infusion recalls the first, and "most Yharnamites are heavy users of blood".
Caryll's rune "Communion" stands for the Church itself: blood ministration is the pursuit of communion.
The Church grooms nuns chosen as vessels for blood into Blood Saints. Being treated with their blood is what lends the Church its legitimacy.
Laurence, Willem's student, became the Church's first vicar. In reality he became the first cleric beast: the blood he spread caught up with him.
His successor, Vicar Amelia, still prays to "seek the old blood" and "partake in communion", while warning of the frailty of men.
The Church needed hunters too. Its workshop began with Ludwig, its first hunter, and departed from old Gehrman's techniques to hunt "more terrifying beasts, and perhaps things still worse".
Another arm of the Church: Logarius's executioners, whose garb became the basis of all Church attire. Their story continues in the Cainhurst tour.

title: The Choir and the cosmos
intro: The Church's elite looked up instead of down. A tour of the Choir, the orphans who became its thinkers, and the Great One they met.

steps.note: In the shadow of the Grand Cathedral, an orphanage turned children into "potent unseen thinkers" for the Church. The Choir was born there, and would later split the Church.
The Choir's inquiry began with an encounter at Byrgenwerth, with "abandoned Ebrietas", a Great One. It started a study of the cosmos from inside the labyrinth.
This chalice, the first great one brought back since Byrgenwerth's time, became the Choir's cornerstone and gave it an audience with Ebrietas.
The Choir's epiphany: with our feet on the earth, "might the cosmos be very near us, only just above our heads?"

steps.text: The sky and the cosmos are…
steps.note: A note signed by the Choir sums up their creed in one line.
They tried to reach the outer cosmos with phantasms, and failed. The failure gave them a weapon instead: "failure is the mother of invention".
At the top of the Church stand the Choir, in the Upper Cathedral Ward, and the School of Mensis, in the Unseen Village. The Paleblood tour picks up Mensis.

title: Mensis and the Nightmare of Mensis
intro: The other half of the Church's elite. A tour of the School of Mensis, its kidnappers, its iron cages, and the dream it chose never to leave.

steps.note: The Healing Church has two upper echelons: the Choir in the Upper Cathedral Ward, and "the School of Mensis, based in the Unseen Village".
Mensis pursues Byrgenwerth's old goal. Master Willem "sought to line his brain with eyes in order to elevate his thoughts". (Tour: Byrgenwerth and the Old Blood.)
Yahar'gul, the Unseen Village, was founded by Mensis, and its hunters answer to the School. They are "hunters in name only": "these kidnappers wear their black hoods low to shadow their eyes".

The School wore these cages to restrain the self and as "an antenna that facilitates contact with the Great Ones of the dream". To an observer, the cage "appears to be precisely what delivered them to their harrowing nightmare".
Caryll's rune explains why contact seemed possible: "The Great Ones that inhabit the nightmare are sympathetic in spirit, and often answer when called upon."

steps.text: Micolash, Host of the Nightmare — passage 1
steps.note: Micolash, the School's host, now lives inside that dream. "The sacred rite nears completion. The dream will be real! We will be granted eyes!" He prays to Kos, "as you once did for the vacuous Rom".

steps.text: Micolash, Host of the Nightmare — passage 2
steps.note: "Plant eyes on our brains, to cleanse our beastly idiocy." He mentions "the grand lake of mud, hidden now, from sight", and refuses to wake: "No, we shall not abandon the dream."

A hidden lake also appears at Byrgenwerth: Master Willem "left his secret with the lake". The texts never say what the secret is. Linking it to Rom and to Micolash's hidden lake is a reading, not something stated.

What Mensis brought back: "The immense brain that Mensis retrieved from the nightmare was indeed lined with eyes on the inside, but they were of an evil sort, and the brain itself was terribly rotten." It was still "a legitimate Great One".

steps.text: When the red moon hangs low,…
steps.note: Meanwhile, in the waking world, the moon turns red, and the line between man and beast blurs. (Tours: Paleblood and the Moon; Oedon and the Great Ones' children.)

title: The scourge of beasts
intro: Why is Yharnam full of beasts, and who hunts them? A tour of the plague, the burning of a district, and what the hunt does to hunters.

steps.text: When the hunt began, the Healing…
steps.note: A note from Old Yharnam: when the hunt began, the Church blocked the bridge to the Cathedral Ward, and Old Yharnam burned that moonlit night.
That fire was a "fiery cleansing" of the scourge. Hunters in fire-resistant capes then hunted the survivors through the flames.
Djura, an old hunter, now guards the burned district and its beasts against other hunters: "they are of no harm to those above".
Yharnam is not the first: the land of Loran was devoured by the sands, a tragedy rooted in the scourge, and "Yharnam may be next".
The Church experimented with controlling the scourge. The failed rune became forbidden, yet "this knowledge became a foundation of the Healing Church".
Hunters are not safe either: a hunter who goes drunk with blood is taken by the Nightmare, to hunt forever.
So some hunters hunt hunters: the Hunters of Hunters, who take the lives of comrades "addled with blood".
The human cost, in one object: a music box from a little girl, with her parents' names inside, Viola and Gascoigne. Gascoigne is a hunter.

title: Cainhurst and the Vilebloods
intro: A forsaken castle, a queen who cannot die, and the Church's executioners who slaughtered her court.

steps.note: An invitation to the forsaken Castle Cainhurst, "rather bafflingly" addressed to you.
The queen's royal guards wield the Chikage, a blade that sings when soaked in blood and eats away at its wielder.
The Vilebloods hunt hunters for the dregs in their blood. Queen Annalise partakes in these offerings, to one day bear "the Child of Blood".
The Church answered with Logarius's band of executioners, who used these wheels to slaughter the Vilebloods.
Logarius then donned the old king's crown himself, "to prevent a single soul from stumbling upon the vile secret".
What remains of Annalise: a warm lump of flesh. "All hail the undying queen of blood!"
Logarius's legacy lives on in Alfred, his self-declared protégé, still hunting Vilebloods.

title: The Hunter's Nightmare
intro: The Old Hunters DLC: where blood-drunk hunters end up, and the secret the Church buried there.

steps.note: Simon explains where you are: the Hunter's Nightmare, "where hunters end up when drunk with blood".
Ludwig, the Church's first hunter, found this arcane sword, whose guidance is "of a very private, elusive sort".
Lady Maria, a hunter and a distant relative of Cainhurst's queen, one day threw her beloved blade into a well, "when she could stomach its presence no longer".
Maria guards the Astral Clocktower. Her words hint at the Church's secret and the "ailing wards" nearby.
The Research Hall's patients call for Lady Maria, hear water, and feel their brains melting.
What the Church's research made of them: heads that expanded "until that was all that they were".
Beyond lies the Fishing Hamlet, on the coast where the carcass of Kos washed up, teeming with parasites.
The hamlet's priest names the culprits, "Byrgenwerth... blood-crazed fiends", and curses them "and their children, and their children's children, for evermore".

title: Paleblood and the Moon
intro: You came to Yharnam seeking Paleblood. A tour of the clues: notes, a dream, and the moon that hangs over it.

steps.note: Gilbert, a fellow outsider, has never heard of Paleblood, and warns you to leave: "This town is cursed".

steps.text: Seek Paleblood to transcend the hunt.
steps.note: A handwritten scrawl that sets the goal of the whole game.
The Hunter's Dream is a former workshop and "safe haven for hunters", kept by old Gehrman, the first hunter.
The Doll, "here in this dream to look after you", turns the echoes of blood into strength.
The Third Umbilical Cord "precipitated the encounter with the pale moon, which beckoned the hunters and conceived the Hunter's Dream".

steps.text: The nameless moon presence beckoned by…
steps.note: Another note puts a name on it: the moon presence beckoned by Laurence and his associates is Paleblood.

steps.text: When the red moon hangs low,…
steps.note: When the moon turns red, "the line between man and beast is blurred", and the Great Ones descend.

steps.text: Micolash, Host of the Nightmare — passage 1
steps.note: The School of Mensis pursues the same dream: "We will be granted eyes!", praying to Kos as it once did for "the vacuous Rom".

title: Oedon and the Great Ones' children
intro: Every Great One loses its child. A tour of that loss and the surrogates it calls for: a formless god, a woman in the Cathedral Ward, a queen, and a sea god's orphan.

steps.note: "Every infant Great One has this precursor to the umbilical cord. Every Great One loses its child, and then yearns for a surrogate."
In the old labyrinth, the remains of failed births: "Stillborn infants born of a creature of unknown origin".
Oedon is a Great One without form: he "exists only in voice". His essence is blood, "a medium of the highest grade".
"Both Oedon, and his inadvertent worshippers, surreptitiously seek the precious blood." Oedon Chapel, at the heart of the Cathedral Ward, bears his name.
Arianna gives her blood to hunters. "A member of the old Healing Church would know that her blood is similar indeed, to precisely what was once forbidden."
Late in the night, she falls ill: "It hurts... my stomach, it hurts terribly..."
"Oh, horrors... Was this born of me? It can't be... this is a nightmare. Ohh, my baby..." The text never names the father. Reading it as Oedon's child comes from the steps before and the next one.

steps.text: When the red moon hangs low,…
steps.note: The note that matches her story: "And when the Great Ones descend, a womb will be blessed with child."
Cainhurst's queen is another would-be mother: Annalise is called "carrier of the Child of Blood". (Tour: Cainhurst and the Vilebloods.)
At the Fishing Hamlet, the loss was a crime: "Mother is dead, her baby, taken. Scales are suffering, the grief of Kos." (Tour: The Hunter's Nightmare.)
The tour ends with the only child set free: "Ahh, sweet child of Kos, returned to the ocean..." Mergo, the infant at the heart of Mensis's nightmare, appears in no text on this map.
